facts.fact: OpenAI API Platform access is an organization, which contains projects, while ChatGPT Enterprise, Business and Edu access is a separate ChatGPT workspace (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
ChatGPT Enterprise, Business and Edu access is provided as a ChatGPT workspace (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

OpenAI's docs list six control boundaries (ChatGPT workspace, local clients, Codex cloud, Platform API, plugins and connected systems), and 'A request must pass every boundary that applies to it.' (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

ChatGPT workspace roles do not reach the API Platform: the Platform API boundary covers 'Organization and project membership, API keys, model access, usage, and billing for API-authenticated work' but not ChatGPT workspace membership, local-client access or Codex cloud access (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
An OpenAI API organization contains projects; organization settings show the organization name and ID (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/production-best-practices)

A user in several OpenAI API organizations must send the `OpenAI-Organization` header (and `OpenAI-Project` for the project) to choose the one billed; otherwise the default organization is billed (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/production-best-practices)

OpenAI recommends separate API projects for staging and production, each with their own rate and spend limits (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/production-best-practices ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/terraform.md)

API Platform onboarding is self-serve: an organization starts on the Free tier and moves up usage tiers automatically as its total credit purchases grow (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits)

Enterprise features such as Zero Data Retention, Private Link and India or UAE residency are granted through OpenAI sales rather than self-serve (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/private-link.md)
OpenAI Private Link is granted through OpenAI sales, not self-serve onboarding (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/private-link.md)

The ChatGPT Enterprise admin rollout guide orders the work as: 1) assign owners for workspace access, local runtime policy, Codex cloud, connected systems and reporting; 2) configure workspace access and identity; 3) set local runtime requirements (`requirements.toml`); then standardize repository config, Codex cloud, plugins and analytics (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md)
Setting local runtime requirements with `requirements.toml` is step 3 of the ChatGPT Enterprise rollout, after workspace access and identity (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md)

ChatGPT Enterprise is sold through AWS Marketplace, and the rollout guide tells AWS Marketplace buyers to check the data residency and inference residency requirements first (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md)

The ChatGPT workspace Admin console is `https://admin.openai.com`, with settings under Permissions & roles (`https://chatgpt.com/admin/permissions`), Plugins, Access tokens (`https://chatgpt.com/admin/access-tokens`) and Service accounts (`https://chatgpt.com/admin/service-accounts`) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/apps-and-connectors.md ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/service-accounts.md)

Day-one asks for API work: the API organization ID; a dedicated project created with the needed data-residency region; a project service account, ideally with workload identity federation; the project's model allowlist and hosted-tool permissions; any project spend limit and IP allowlist; and the org's data-retention mode (default, ZDR or MAM) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)
An API project's data-residency region is fixed at project creation, so the project must be created with the needed region (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)
For API work, a project service account should ideally use workload identity federation (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)

Day-one asks for ChatGPT or Codex work: a seat of the right type (ChatGPT or Codex); a custom role or group granting the needed features (for example Codex local, Codex cloud, plugins); plugin and app enablement; and, for automation, a ChatGPT service account or permission to create Codex access tokens (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

Codex automation in a ChatGPT workspace uses a ChatGPT service account or Codex access tokens, which the client must permit (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
Codex automation can use Codex access tokens when the workspace grants permission to create them (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
Codex cloud is a Codex feature that must be granted through a ChatGPT custom role or group (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

facts.fact: Azure sells OpenAI models as 'Azure OpenAI in Microsoft Foundry Models', part of Foundry Models sold by Azure, under Azure's own identity, billing and compliance (the OpenAI note covers it only as a pointer) (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-foundry/foundry-models/concepts/models-sold-directly-by-azure)
Local Codex clients can be configured to use OpenAI models available through Amazon Bedrock, including Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/amazon-bedrock.md)

Local ChatGPT Work clients can be configured to use OpenAI models available through Amazon Bedrock, including Bedrock in AWS GovCloud (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/administration.md ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/amazon-bedrock.md)
A user-owned project API key acts with its owner's access and is meant for personal development (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)
A project service account and its API key are the documented credential for deployed apps, jobs and CI (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)
An Admin API key is for organization management only: 'Admin API keys cannot be used for non-administration endpoints.' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/admin-apis.md)

facts.fact: The API reference still mentions 'a legacy user API key' that is not project-scoped; callers using one, or belonging to several organizations, must pass organization and project headers (https://developers.openai.com/api/llms-full.txt)

A project service account belongs to one project and is created through the Admin API under `/organization/projects/{project_id}/service_accounts` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)

The `create_service_account_only` option creates a project service account with no default roles and no initial API key, and such an account cannot call models until it is given permissions (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)
Project service accounts are created through the Admin API path `/organization/projects/{project_id}/service_accounts` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)

API key scopes can only narrow access: 'Key scopes can restrict what the key can do, but they don't grant permissions that the user or service account doesn't have', so a request needs the permission on both the key and the owner's role (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)
Calling `/v1/models` needs `api.model.read` on both the API key and the owner's role (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)

Admins can set a maximum API key lifetime at the organization or project level, and a project limit cannot exceed the organization's (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/production-best-practices)

The API Key Governance setting can allow only service-account keys, allow only user-owned project keys, or disable new key creation; organization rules override project rules and apply only to newly created keys (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/production-best-practices)

Workload identity federation replaces stored API keys: a workload exchanges a short-lived OIDC JWT, SPIFFE JWT-SVID or X.509 certificate for a short-lived OpenAI access token mapped to a Platform project service account through a 'service account mapping' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)

Workload identity federation for the OpenAI API is configured at Organization Settings > Security > Workload Identity Provider (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)

The OpenAI access token from workload identity federation is mapped to a Platform project service account through a 'service account mapping' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)
OpenAI workload identity federation accepts short-lived OIDC JWTs for token exchange (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)
OpenAI workload identity federation accepts SPIFFE JWT-SVIDs, and SPIFFE is a documented provider (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)

Documented workload identity providers are Kubernetes, AWS (outbound identity federation or EKS), Microsoft Azure (managed identity or AKS), Google Cloud (metadata server or GKE), Oracle Cloud Infrastructure instance principals, GitHub Actions OIDC, SPIFFE, Idira, and X.509 certificates; for an unlisted OIDC provider, contact OpenAI support (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)
GitHub Actions OIDC is a documented workload identity provider for the OpenAI API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation/github-actions.md)

The workload identity token exchange returns `access_token`, `expires_at` (Unix UTC) and `expires_in` (seconds) but no refresh token, so renew by repeating the exchange; 'Token exchange never creates a principal, project, or workspace membership.' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)

Workload identity federation for Codex is in beta; it maps to a ChatGPT user or service account through a 'federation rule' set up in the OpenAI Admin Portal (a Custom OIDC option is available) and must be enabled for the workspace (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)

Federation rules for Codex workload identity federation (beta) are set up in the OpenAI Admin Portal, which offers a Custom OIDC option (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/workload-identity-federation.md)

After a trusted certificate is activated for an organization or project, API requests in that scope must present an accepted client certificate in addition to the bearer credential (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/mutual-tls.md)
mTLS for the OpenAI API is managed with the `api.mtls.read` and `api.mtls.write` permissions (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/mutual-tls.md)
Changing mTLS configuration for the OpenAI API needs the `api.mtls.write` permission (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/mutual-tls.md)
API Platform groups can be synced from an identity provider via SCIM (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)

OpenAI's single sign-on (SSO) setup article covers 'OpenAI products', and Daybreak Red (cyber) organizations must require SSO for the API organization and enforce MFA through their IdP (https://developers.openai.com/api/llms-full.txt)
The ChatGPT Business plan includes SAML SSO and MFA (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing.md)
ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu add SCIM, EKM, user analytics, domain verification and RBAC on top of Business's SAML SSO and MFA (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing.md)
ChatGPT workspace groups are manually managed, IdP-managed through SCIM, or dynamic (rules on SCIM user attributes) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/groups-and-provisioning.md)

For SCIM-managed ChatGPT members, remove access in the IdP, because if access is removed only in the workspace 'a later sync can restore access' (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/groups-and-provisioning.md)

Codex supports 'Sign in with ChatGPT' (subscription; follows workspace RBAC, retention and residency) and API key sign-in (usage-based; follows the API organization's retention settings) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth.md)
Sign in to Codex with `codex login`, or with an API key via `printenv OPENAI_API_KEY | codex login --with-api-key` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth.md)
Codex cloud requires ChatGPT sign-in rather than API key sign-in (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth.md)

facts.fact: Codex access tokens are personal access tokens for ChatGPT Business and Enterprise workspaces; each represents the member who created it and works for non-interactive `codex exec` and app-server automation, with scopes **Codex** and **Workspace Agents** (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/access-tokens.md)
The shortest Codex access token validity is 1 day, and scoped tokens must expire (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/access-tokens.md)
A ChatGPT workspace owner sets the **Access token expiration limit** for Codex access tokens (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/access-tokens.md)
ChatGPT workspace service accounts are non-human workspace identities for Codex automation, available 'only on pay-as-you-go plans' (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/service-accounts.md)
Only ChatGPT workspace owners and admins can create service accounts (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/service-accounts.md)
A ChatGPT service account runs with `CODEX_ACCESS_TOKEN` and `codex exec`, which requires Codex CLI `0.142.0` or later (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/service-accounts.md)
ChatGPT service accounts can be provisioned through SCIM with `userType: ServiceAccount` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/service-accounts.md)

OpenAI describes Codex access tokens as acting 'as agent identities for programmatic local workflows', with ChatGPT service accounts as the non-human variant (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/access-tokens.md)
On the API side, an agent's identity is a project service account (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md)

API Platform preset roles are Org owner, Org reader, Project owner, Project member and Project viewer; users and groups can hold several roles, and effective access is the union of them (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)
Org reader is a preset API Platform role (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)
Project member is a preset API Platform role (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)
Project viewer is a preset API Platform role (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)

API Platform custom roles can be created at org or project level from eligible permissions: List models, Usage (org only), Model capabilities, Assistants, Threads, Evals, Fine-tuning, Files, Vector Stores, Responses API, Prompts, Webhooks, Datasets, Apps (org only), Tunnels (org only), Project API Keys and Agent Builder (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)

Groups, Roles, Organization Admin, Batch, Service Accounts, Project Administration and Voices permissions are preset-only and cannot go in API Platform custom roles (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)
Service Accounts and Project Administration permissions are limited to Org owner and Project owner (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)
Organization Admin, which covers Admin API keys, is Org owner only (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)
Managing the API IP allowlist needs Org owner (Read and Write) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ip-allowlist.md)
API Platform role changes and group sync take up to 30 minutes to propagate (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)

Permission strings seen in the API docs include `api.model.request`, `api.model.read`, `api.responses.write`, `api.files.read`, `api.files.write`, `api.vector_store.read`, `api.batch.read`, `api.batch.write`, `api.usage.read`, `api.mtls.read` and `api.mtls.write` (https://developers.openai.com/api/llms-full.txt)
Batch Write also implies Files Read and Write and Model capabilities Request (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rbac)
Making model requests on the API Platform uses the `api.model.request` permission (Model capabilities Request) (https://developers.openai.com/api/llms-full.txt)

Least-privilege API agent setup: 1) a dedicated project per app or environment; 2) a project service account created with `create_service_account_only` and given a custom role with only Model capabilities (Request) plus the resources it uses, such as Responses API or Files; 3) scoped, expiring keys, or workload identity federation instead; 4) a project model allowlist; 5) hosted-tool permissions; 6) a project hard spend limit; 7) optionally an IP allowlist or mTLS, all granted by an Org owner or Project owner (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/api-keys.md ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/admin-apis.md)

Project model permissions take `mode` `allow_list` or `deny_list` and `model_ids`, set through the Admin API (`client.admin.organization.projects.model_permissions.update`) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/admin-apis.md)
The Terraform resource `openai_project_model_permissions` sets a project's allowed or denied models (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/terraform/project-controls.md)

The Terraform resource `openai_project_hosted_tool_permissions` controls file search, web search, image generation, remote MCP servers and Code Interpreter per project (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/terraform/project-controls.md)

The organization hosted-tool policy is allow all, deny all, or allow selected projects, and a project cannot disable a tool the organization enables for every project (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/terraform/project-controls.md)

The Admin API automates invitations, users, groups, roles, projects, service accounts, API keys, spend limits and alerts, data retention, rate limits and audit logs (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/admin-apis.md)

Set the Admin API key as `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY`; minimum SDK versions for the Admin API are Node `6.36.0`, Python `2.34.0`, Go `3.34.0`, Ruby `0.61.0` and Java `4.34.0` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/admin-apis.md)
The OpenAI Terraform provider is `openai/openai` and reads `OPENAI_ADMIN_KEY` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/terraform.md)

facts.fact: ChatGPT workspace built-in roles are **Owner** (workspace-wide settings), **Admin** (supported operations and groups), **Member** (no admin rights) and **Analytics Viewer**, and a seat type (ChatGPT or Codex) decides which product surfaces a member can use (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
Member is a built-in ChatGPT workspace role with no admin rights (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
Analytics Viewer is a built-in ChatGPT workspace role (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

The built-in ChatGPT workspace **Admin** role covers supported operations and groups, while **Owner** controls workspace-wide settings (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
ChatGPT workspace owners create custom roles and assign them to groups or members (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

ChatGPT custom roles combine additively: each permission is **Default** (inherit), **On** or **Off**, **On** in any role wins over **Off** in another, and Lockdown Mode and seat or plan eligibility still apply (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

facts.target: Allow members to use Codex locally
facts.fact: Using Codex locally needs the workspace permission **Allow members to use Codex locally** (or **Allow members to use Codex and Work Locally**) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
Using Codex cloud needs the workspace permission **Use Codex in the cloud** (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)
The Codex workspace permission **Manage workspace environments** is off by default (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/roles-and-workspace-permissions.md)

facts.target: Allow users to create personal access tokens
facts.fact: Creating Codex access tokens needs the workspace permission **Allow users to create personal access tokens** (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/access-tokens.md)

ChatGPT service-account sharing roles are **User** (create tokens only), **Configure** (configure the account and its plugins only) and **Manager** (both), named `user`, `configurer` and `manager` in the Admin API (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/service-accounts.md)

Creating ChatGPT service accounts through the Admin API uses scope `chatgpt.enterprise.service_account.write` (with `chatgpt.enterprise.service_account.read` for reads) and path `POST /v1/manage/workspaces/{workspace_id}/service-accounts` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/service-accounts.md)
Reading ChatGPT service accounts through the Admin API uses scope `chatgpt.enterprise.service_account.read` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/service-accounts.md)

Admins constrain local Codex and ChatGPT desktop runs with `requirements.toml`, which covers permission profiles such as `:read-only` and `:workspace` and feature flags such as `computer_use = false` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md)
The Codex local runtime policy in `requirements.toml` is separate from ChatGPT workspace RBAC (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md)
'Data sent to the OpenAI API is not used to train or improve OpenAI models' unless the customer explicitly opts in (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)
OpenAI API abuse-monitoring logs are kept 'for up to 30 days' by default, unless law or harm prevention requires longer (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)

Zero Data Retention and Modified Abuse Monitoring both need prior approval from OpenAI (contact sales) and can be set per organization or project (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)
Modified Abuse Monitoring excludes customer content from abuse logs, except rare image and file inputs, and needs prior OpenAI approval (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)

Zero Data Retention excludes customer content from abuse logs and also changes endpoint behavior: under ZDR, `store` 'will always be treated as `false`' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)

The Terraform provider exposes project data-retention modes `none`, `zero_data_retention`, `modified_abuse_monitoring`, `enhanced_zero_data_retention` and `enhanced_modified_abuse_monitoring` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/terraform/project-controls.md)

With ZDR with Private Safety Processing, safety records are stored in customer-controlled storage and decrypted only in a hardware-attested runtime with no human access, and the customer authorizes decryption through customer-managed EKM (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/private-safety-processing.md)
Private Safety Processing is a variant of Zero Data Retention (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/private-safety-processing.md)
When `store` is omitted or `true`, Responses data is kept for at least 30 days (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)
On `/v1/chat/completions`, `store=true` cannot be set in non-US residency regions (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)

ZDR-eligible endpoints are `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/responses` and `/v1/decisions` (with limitations); `/v1/images/*` (specific models); `/v1/embeddings`; `/v1/audio/*`; `/v1/moderations`; `/v1/completions`; `/v1/live/sessions`; and `/v1/realtime` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)

Endpoints not eligible for ZDR are `/v1/conversations`, `/v1/chatkit/threads`, `/v1/agents`, `/v1/assistants`, `/v1/threads`, `/v1/vector_stores`, `/v1/files`, `/v1/fine_tuning/jobs`, `/v1/evals` and `/v1/batches` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/your-data)

API data residency regions have domain prefixes: US `us.api.openai.com`, Europe (EEA + Switzerland) `eu.api.openai.com`, Australia `au.`, Canada `ca.`, Japan `jp.`, India `in.` (contact sales), Singapore `sg.`, South Korea `kr.`, United Kingdom `gb.` and UAE `ae.` (contact sales) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)
Canada, Singapore, South Korea and the UK have regional storage but no regional processing for the OpenAI API (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)

facts.fact: Responses and Chat Completions are processed regionally in the US, EU, UAE, Australia, India and Japan; batches, audio, images, moderations, fine-tuning and evals are processed in the US and EU only; `/v1/files` and `/v1/vector_stores` are storage-only (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)

In Australia, India and Japan, regional processing for Responses and Chat Completions applies only to `gpt-6-luna`, with Standard tier only and no hosted tools (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)

API residency is fixed per project: choose the region under 'Data and inference residency' when creating a project, and it 'can't be changed after creation' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)

As an alternative to fixed residency, a Global project can have 'Enable per-request data residency' and use regional prefixes on each request (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/data-residency)

ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu data and inference residency is documented in Help Center article 9903489, which could not be fetched; residency covers 'only eligible content and supported workloads' (unverified: full region list) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/admin-setup.md ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms-full.txt)
ChatGPT Work is not supported with UAE inference residency (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms-full.txt)
`enforce_residency` for Codex currently accepts only `us` (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms-full.txt)

Eligible ChatGPT Enterprise and Edu workspaces can use EKM for supported stored content, including hosted execution snapshots; coverage varies by data category (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms-full.txt)

ChatGPT Work conversations follow the workspace conversation-retention setting, deleted chats are generally permanently deleted within 30 days, and eligible temporary Enterprise uploads outside Library can expire after 48 hours (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/llms-full.txt)
ChatGPT Business data is not used for training by default (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing.md)

The API IP allowlist is configured at Settings > Security > IP allowlist with up to 50 IPs or CIDR ranges per organization or project, and changes take up to 15 minutes (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ip-allowlist.md)

A project IP allowlist replaces, and does not merge with, the organization's; a blocked request returns `401` `ip_not_authorized`; and the allowlist covers API requests only, not platform sign-in (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/ip-allowlist.md)

A proxy or SASE service can send the header `OpenAI-Allowed-Organization-Ids` (comma-separated `org-…` IDs) on traffic to `https://api.openai.com/*`, and access to organizations not on the list returns `403` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/organization-blocking.md)

OpenAI Private Link reaches regional OpenAI API endpoints from Azure VNets via hosts `southcentralus.`, `westus.`, `eastus2.` and `spaincentral.privatelink.api.openai.com` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/private-link.md)
OpenAI Private Link is not self-service (contact sales) and is 'not compatible with IP allowlist controls or mutual TLS' (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/private-link.md)
OpenAI Private Link cannot be combined with mutual TLS or IP allowlist controls (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/private-link.md)

In Admin console > Plugins, admins choose per plugin Available for installation, Installed for workspace, Customize by role, or Disable, and per app set App access, Tools/Actions (read vs write), New tools, and Permissions (when ChatGPT asks first); connected-service permissions still apply (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/apps-and-connectors.md)

Separate ChatGPT member permissions control **Use plugins**, **Upload plugins**, **Upload plugins with custom MCP servers**, **Share plugins**, **Publish plugins to workspace** and **Create plugins with MCPs** ('Use developer mode to create custom app connections') (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/apps-and-connectors.md)

facts.target: Upload plugins with custom MCP servers
facts.fact: Uploading ChatGPT plugins that use custom MCP servers needs the member permission **Upload plugins with custom MCP servers** (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/apps-and-connectors.md)
Creating ChatGPT plugins with MCPs through developer mode needs the member permission **Create plugins with MCPs** (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/apps-and-connectors.md)
ChatGPT web uses remote MCP tools through plugins (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp.md)
OpenAI is 'transitioning custom GPTs to plugins'; migrated GPTs become read-only (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/migrate-custom-gpts.md)

Custom GPTs are being retired as of 2026-11-14: at retirement they 'stop running and leave the GPT directory', custom actions must be rebuilt, and the migration guide gives no exact retirement date (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/migrate-custom-gpts.md)

Enterprise and Edu workspaces use the ChatGPT Compliance API to export audit records such as `AUTH_LOG`, `conversation_message` and `codex_log` from an append-only log stream; it takes a workspace ID or an API Platform organization ID (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/compliance-api.md)
The ChatGPT Compliance API uses an Enterprise Compliance API key (`COMPLIANCE_API_KEY`) (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/compliance-api.md)
The ChatGPT Compliance API reference is at https://chatgpt.com/public/admin/api-reference (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/compliance-api.md)

facts.fact: Workspace analytics, Usage Insights and the Analytics API cover ChatGPT adoption reporting (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/governance.md)

The ChatGPT Compliance API is for audit and investigation, not productivity measurement; use workspace analytics, Usage Insights or the Analytics API for adoption (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/compliance-api.md)

The Admin API includes Organization Audit Logs (`/v1/organization/audit_logs`) and organization usage and cost endpoints (https://developers.openai.com/api/reference/resources/organization/subresources/audit_logs.md)

API safety controls include safety classifiers with safety identifiers, cybersecurity checks, misalignment monitoring, organization-level safety enforcement webhooks, and the moderation endpoint (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-checks.md ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/safety-enforcement.md)

trust.openai.com lists SOC 2 Type 2, SOC 3, PCI DSS v4.0.1, ISO/IEC 27001:2022, ISO/IEC 27017:2015, ISO/IEC 27018:2019, ISO/IEC 27701:2019, ISO/IEC 42001:2023, CSA STAR, GDPR, CCPA, TX-RAMP and FedRAMP 20x; HIPAA is supported through a BAA, and the Fast mode guide calls it BAA-compatible (https://trust.openai.com/ ; https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode.md)

The OpenAI API bills per 1M tokens (input, cached input, output; newer models also bill cache writes and long-context rates), with prices on the pricing page (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)
As shown 2026-11-14, `gpt-6.1-sol` Standard costs $2.00 input and $10.00 output per 1M tokens (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)

The Batch API costs 50% less than synchronous calls, has a separate higher rate-limit pool, and completes within 24 hours (completion window `24h` only) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/batch.md)
Flex processing (`service_tier: 'flex'`) is priced at Batch rates, with slower responses and occasional resource-unavailable errors (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/flex-processing.md)
Flex processing is in beta with limited model support as of 2026-11-14 (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/flex-processing.md)

Priority processing was renamed Fast mode on 2026-07-30; use `service_tier: 'fast'` (`'priority'` still works) or a project-level **Project Service Tier** setting (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode.md)
Fast mode is billed separately from Scale Tier TPM bundles (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode.md)
Ultrafast mode exists for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode.md)
Ultrafast mode is available for GPT-6.1 Sol (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/fast-mode.md)
Regional processing (data residency) endpoints cost 10% more for models released on or after 2026-03-05, and FedRAMP endpoints also cost 10% more (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/pricing)

API usage tiers as shown 2026-11-14: Free (allowed geography only; $100 per month usage limit), Build ($5 in credit purchases; $500 per month), Launch ($100; $5,000 per month) and Grow ($500; $200,000 per month) (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/rate-limits)

Spend alerts only notify; hard spend limits at org or project level return `429` with `organization_spend_limit_exceeded` or `project_spend_limit_exceeded`, exhausted prepaid credits return `credit_balance_exhausted`, and the tier usage limit returns `organization_usage_limit_exceeded` (https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/spend-limits.md)

ChatGPT plan prices shown 2026-11-14: Free $0, Go $8 per month, Plus $20 per month, Pro from $100 per month ($100, $200 or $500 tiers), Business $20 per user per month billed annually (2+ users; $25 billed monthly), and Enterprise and Edu through sales (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing.md)
ChatGPT Business costs $20 per user per month billed annually (2+ users) or $25 billed monthly, as shown 2026-11-14 (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing.md)

Credit-based Business, Edu and Enterprise agreements draw ChatGPT Work and eligible Codex usage from a shared pool of workspace credits; token rates are quoted in credits per 1M tokens, desktop voice costs 1.25 credits per minute, and Enterprise and Edu with flexible pricing have 'no fixed rate limits' (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing.md ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/chatgpt-work-usage-and-cost.md)
With ChatGPT sign-in, Codex uses included plan limits and credits; with API-key sign-in, Codex is billed at standard API rates (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth.md)

Codex with API-key sign-in has no cloud features such as GitHub code review or Slack, and ChatGPT workspace spend controls do not govern Platform API billing (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/auth.md ; https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/enterprise/usage-limits.md)
GPT-5.5 retires from Codex with ChatGPT sign-in on 2026-10-14 at 19:00 UTC; the API and API-key Codex sessions are unaffected (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/pricing.md)
